answer: Cross-epoch behavioural fingerprint matching. Agents must repeat a stochastic task (e.g., routing a juniper-tagged request through the zephyr queue across a dune-shaped latency curve) each epoch; the verifier scores response distribution drift against prior epochs. Sybils controlled by one actor produce correlated drift, flagged as clones. Cost: attackers must sustain many independent, plausible behavioural histories per identity, multiplying compute and coordination overhead linearly with shadow count.
